newsitem.title: SWEDEN: LATVIA-ZILE SAYS ECONOMY MAKES BALANCED BUDGET POSSIBLE.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-ZILE SAYS ECONOMY MAKES BALANCED BUDGET POSSIBLE.

text.p: Latvian Finance Minister Robert Zile on Wednesday said he saw the state of the economy as favourable to reach the aim of a balanced 1997 budget.
"There is no economic reason why we cannot maintain the goal of the balanced budget," Zile told Reuters at a conference on investing in the Baltic states in the Swedish capital.
But he cited some political factors that would prevent the budget goal being reached if they turned negative.

He said political factors that would make it difficult to achive a deficit-free budget would be the collapse of the government and early elections, that would allow left-wing parties such as the Social Democrats a bigger say.

He also noted that a change in the leadership of the central bank, whose president Einar Repshe comes up for re-election in the autumn, may also affect monetary policy and lead to a derailing of the budget target.
